rules.sentence: Spontaneous closure of the ductus is very rare after the first three months of birth.
In all adults, the presence of a ductus requires surgical closure.
Before the ductus is closed in the adult population, the status of the pulmonary vasculature must be determined.
Thus, patients with mild pulmonary hypertension have a normal life expectancy.
The surgical mortality for ductus varies from 2-20% depending on the infant's age and other co-existing comorbidities.
If left untreated, the mortality rate increases with age.
If PFO persists into adulthood, it usually leads to right-to-left shunting of deoxygenated blood, which can be symptomatic or asymptomatic.
Additionally, if a PFO is present and venous thromboembolism (VTE) develops, the PFO can lead to shunting of the VTE into the arterial circulation.
